newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal-Offers weak on lackluster demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal-Offers weak on lackluster demand.

text.p: Offers for soymeal in U.S. cash markets were mostly unchanged Monday, but some offers fell on ongoing lackluster demand, dealers said.
"A lot of them (end-users) are waiting for prices to go lower," said one dealer.
However, some see a jump in the pace of U.S. exports if prices continue to fall.
"The export market is looking pretty good right now," said one dealer in the southeast.
Traders in export channels said that little was moving on the rivers, but business could be expected in August.
Asian traders said China was expected to buy 50,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal if values continued to slide, and South Korea was seen looking for 40,000 tonnes of soymeal for September/October shipment.

The National Oilseed Processors Association released crushing data for the week ended July 2 on Monday. NOPA put the crush at 24.386 million bushels, within trade expectations for 23.9 million to 24.5 million bushels. The crush data was delayed because of the Independence Day holiday on Friday, July 4.
